clue.text: Chief upset when it's announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word for upset is heard rather than read

parts.note: to upset someone is to shake them

explanation.surface: A boss becomes agitated whenever a particular piece of news is broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab sheikh is the head of a tribe or family, a chief.

clue.text: One house going up after another leads to a commotion

indicators.note: after means the reversed pair is placed following another house

parts.note: another house, HO again

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: one is the indefinite article a

explanation.surface: Houses built one after another lead to an outcry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' reverses A + HO to OHA, which follows a second HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a fuss or commotion.

clue.text: Regularly isn't seeing that religious teaching is hypocritical

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word that follows

parts.note: seeing that means since
RE is religious education, taught in British schools

explanation.surface: A person who often doesn't see that church teaching condemns false piety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' picks the 1st and 3rd letters of isn't, I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: An insincere person says what they do not feel, which is hypocritical.

clue.text: Fools almost killed bug

parts.note: to have someone is to fool them, so fools gives has

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: slew is the past tense of slay, killed

explanation.surface: Idiots very nearly wiped out an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fools' looks like a noun but is a verb: you've been had means you've been fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to pester them, to hassle them.

clue.text: Lover, desperate chap, going to perform courtship dance

parts.note: a fan is a lover or devotee of something
Desperate Dan is the strongman cowboy of the British children's comic The Dandy
to be going is to go, the verb in its plain form

explanation.surface: An eager suitor, a hopeless fellow, sets off to perform a dance to woo someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a famous character from the British comic The Dandy, so 'desperate chap' gives DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish dance for a couple, traditionally one of courtship.

clue.text: Overcoming resistance, charge society for psychoanalytic technique

indicators.note: overcoming means covering, so the charge goes round the resistance

parts.note: a fee is a charge
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
an association is a society or club

explanation.surface: A therapist who gets past a patient's resistance charges a group for a method of analysis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overcoming' puts FEE round R to give FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Free association, from Freud, has the patient say whatever comes to mind as a technique of psychoanalysis.

clue.text: Harry Truman is assuming nothing!

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: President Harry Truman is presuming nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like Truman's first name but is the anagram signal; 'assuming' means putting on, as clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturism is the practice of going naked, putting on no clothes.

clue.text: Unmarried woman's slang

indicators.note: M is the abbreviation for married, so unmarried takes an M away

parts.note: Margot is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A spinster's way of talking in slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unmarried' looks like an adjective for the woman; it removes M (married) from MARGOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the jargon or slang of a particular group.

clue.text: Plant under logs growing wild

indicators.note: something growing wild is unruly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant spreads freely beneath fallen logs.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common weed of the daisy family.

clue.text: Agree about one's temperature not changing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for agree goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to agree is to consent
one is I, and one's is read as I'S

explanation.surface: People concur that a reading of temperature stays steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' reads as I'S, a common crossword trick; 'about' wraps the agreeing verb round it and T, leaving 'not changing' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something consistent is steady and unvarying, the same throughout.

clue.text: Stupid person's chatter

definitions.meaning: a fool or idiot is called a ... in slang
to talk on and on, rabbiting endlessly

explanation.definitionFit: Goon is slang for a dim-witted person, and read as two words it means to talk at length.

clue.text: Tree turning long before start of autumn, in the end

indicators.note: turning says the whole assembly is turned round and read backwards
in places the pieces inside the word for the end

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

indicators.note: before puts the word for long ahead of the first letter of autumn

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: start of picks out the first letter of autumn

explanation.surface: A tree that turns as autumn begins, eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end' means a goal, not a finish; 'in' sets the long-before-A piece within it and 'turning' reverses the lot, giving AILONGAM read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The magnolia is a tree or shrub with large showy flowers.

clue.text: Ordinary seaman or ensign without money

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the flag goes round the cash

parts.note: an ensign is a flag, and rag is slang for a flag
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A lowly sailor or a junior officer who has no cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' tempts as lacking but here means outside, its old sense, so the flag wraps the cash; ensign is the definition's decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Navy a rating is a sailor who is not a commissioned officer.

clue.text: Island has link by bridge at last

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A Scottish island is now connected to the mainland by a bridge at long last.
explanation.walkthrough: The Skye Bridge, opened in 1995, joined the island to the Scottish mainland, so the surface is true.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is a large island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Soundly criticises introduction of liquor in wicked US city

indicators.note: soundly says the word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: to knock is to criticise

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the word for wicked

parts.note: vile means wicked

indicators.note: introduction of picks the first letter of liquor

explanation.surface: Someone strongly condemns bringing alcohol into a sinful American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction of' gives L, which goes 'in' VILE for VILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Knoxville is a city in Tennessee in the United States.

clue.text: Bottom revealed during short nap, very cheeky!

indicators.note: during means within, so the word for bottom goes inside the shortened nap
short means the last letter of the nap is cut off

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon nap
ass is slang for the bottom or backside

explanation.surface: Someone's backside was exposed while they dozed, which was most impertinent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' clips the final A from the nap, leaving SIEST, and 'during' sets the bottom inside; 'revealed' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassy means impudent or cheeky, so the superlative is most cheeky.

clue.text: Crime of one hired before battle at the front is joined possibly

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged letters ahead of the battle's first letter
possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way
at the front picks out the first letter of battle

explanation.surface: A mercenary's offence committed just before battle begins in earnest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the two words into INSIDEJO, placed 'before' the B from 'at the front'; an inside job is done by someone on the payroll.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside job is a crime committed by an employee or insider of the target.

clue.text: Fired up during fight for dagger

indicators.note: during means within, so the reversed word goes inside the fight

parts.note: a set-to is a fight

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: lit means fired or ignited

explanation.surface: Someone angry in a brawl reaches for a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for fired, giving TIL, which goes 'during' the fight; a set-to is British for a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slender blade.

clue.text: Daily row between couple at home

definitions.meaning: a daily is a cleaner who comes to a house each day
a quarrel between partners in a household

explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is both a household servant and a family quarrel, and the clue gives each sense.

clue.text: One reflecting in Paradise Lost

indicators.note: reflecting says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone muses over Milton's epic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden letters ELOS in paradisE LOSt, and 'reflecting' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means one and only, single.

clue.text: Supply new words for Labour leader in capital …

parts.note: to dub a film is to supply new words for it

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A party writes a new speech for the Labour leader in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Dublin is the capital city of Ireland.

clue.text: Assertion made in letter I possibly read out

indicators.note: something read out is spoken, so the phrase is heard and not seen

parts.note: I is one example of a vowel, so the phrase means a vowel

explanation.surface: A statement contained in a letter that is perhaps read aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' tempts as a written letter; it is the alphabet letter I, an example of a vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open declaration or assertion.

clue.text: … Labour shortly being on way to defeat

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece being on another sits above it
shortly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: work is labour
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: The Labour party is soon on course for losing.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 20 down for the surface only. 'to worst' is to defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To worst someone is to get the better of them, to defeat them.

clue.text: Notice worker eating cake that's small and rich

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the notice swallows the cake

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a notice
a bun is a small cake
the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A notice says a labourer is eating a small but very rich cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant means plentiful, rich in supply.

clue.text: Fellow upset about graduate becoming a drifter

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed fellow goes round the graduate
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a college
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A college academic is unsettled by a graduate turning into a wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the college fellow over, giving NOD, and 'about' wraps that round the graduate; a don is a university teacher in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad has no fixed home and moves from place to place, a drifter.

clue.text: To drink noisily, not quietly, is a disgrace

indicators.note: P is piano, quietly in music, so not quietly drops a P

parts.note: to slurp is to drink noisily

explanation.surface: Drinking loudly rather than softly is considered shameful manners.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is a stain on someone's reputation, a disgrace.

clue.text: With (appropriately) clear leap, start this event?

definitions.text: With (appropriately) clear leap, start this event?

parts.words: With (appropriately) clear leap, start this event?
parts.note: clear, leap and start each mean to spring or bound, so three such words fit an athletics event made of three bounds

explanation.walkthrough: Clear, leap and start are three words for one kind of bound, which suits the event: it is a hop, a step and a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: This field event has three bounds in a row, a hop, a step and a final leap into the sandpit.

clue.text: Won't a bed that's made badly be very hot?

indicators.note: a badly made bed is muddled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble that a poorly made bed will be too warm to sleep in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made badly' rearranges WONT and ABED; the sun beats down when it is very hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun is said to beat down when it shines with great heat.

clue.text: Toff oddly taken thus as being without value

parts.note: a nob is a toff, a posh person

indicators.note: taken thus means taken in the way the word itself says, so its odd letters are picked

explanation.surface: A posh man, oddly behaving in this way, is thought to be worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' is fodder: 'taken thus' means take the word oddly in odd fashion, its 1st, 3rd and 5th letters, O, D, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is a person of no importance, a being without value.
